headline: Strong windstorm tonight, then a wet, breezy stretch through much of next week.
summary: A deep Pacific low is pushing a strong cold front across western Washington tonight, bringing widespread rain and gusty winds that peak overnight into early Sunday. The coast faces the worst of the wind and high surf, with a slight chance of thunderstorms mostly near shore. Behind the front, cold air aloft keeps things showery and unsettled, with a series of Pacific storms through the end of the week. Sunday brings a lull in the wind and showers that taper off, with snow in the higher mountains. A brief break Sunday evening gives way to another wet, breezy system Monday, then a steadier moisture stream brings more rain and milder temperatures Tuesday into Wednesday. Forecasters are less certain about the later systems.
changes: The latest update added a slight chance of thunderstorms, mostly near the coast, and raised possible coastal gusts to 55 mph or more. Midweek now looks wetter, with steadier rain Tuesday into Wednesday rather than mainly mild weather.
